test: cut_ending_flush_with_a_side_leaves_no_skin (SolidCraft PR #3327, closed unmerged: main fixed it first with #2827, coplanar::has_skin); own minimal reproduction, the reporter's data is not used
summary: A cut whose tool is flush with a wall (its end face on the plate's side y = 30) and whose top face is tilted by 4e-8 rad off the plate's top face (z = 2) left a skin of thickness ~1e-4 mm on SolidCraft's truck kernel: the near-coplanar boolean failed on every route and only the last-resort tool displacement succeeded, pushing the tool's end into the wall, so the flush cut had one face more than the same cut overshooting the wall by 1 mm (14 against 13 in the PR's test). Geometry: a 60 x 30 x 2 plate united with a 60 x 15 x 10 wall block (y 0..15), cut by the box x 25..35, y 5..y1, z -1..2 rotated by 4e-8 rad (2.29183e-6 degrees) about the axis (0.6, 0.8, 0) through (30, 17.5, 0.5); y1 = 30 is flush, y1 = 31 overshoots. Both variants must give the same solid: a tunnel under the wall block (end wall, two side walls, ceiling) opening into a slot through the plate to the side y = 30. Faces: the L-shaped base has 8 (bottom, y = 0, top z = 10, y = 15, top z = 2, y = 30, x = 0, x = 60); the slot splits each of top z = 2 and y = 30 into two faces (8 + 2 = 10) and the tunnel adds four (end wall, two side walls, ceiling): 14. Volume 10800 - 500 = 10300 mm^3 from the box dimensions, the same for both.

cases.name: flush_with_wall
cases.note: the tool's end face lies on the plate's side y = 30 (the reporter's case; 13 faces with the skin)

volume.formula: plate 60*30*2 = 3600 plus wall 60*15*10 = 9000 minus their overlap 60*15*2 = 1800 gives 10800; the cut removes 10 * 25 * 2 = 500 (x 25..35, y 5..30, z 0..2; the tool's other 1 mm below z = 0 and the overshoot past y = 30 hold no material); tol 0.1 = 1e-5 relative, the rotation moves the volume by about 1e-6

cases.note: the tool passes 1 mm beyond y = 30 (control; 14 faces on the old kernel)
